newsitem.title: UK: Copper steadier but reluctant above $1,970 on LME.
newsitem.headline: Copper steadier but reluctant above $1,970 on LME.

text.p: Copper prices brought the curtain down on a generally low-key LME by sticking a toe in the waters above $1,970, but never looked like extending this move.
But prices still ended steadier and close to Wednesday's highs, injecting an undercurrent of stability to all base metals.
Elsewhere, conditions were sluggish, although there was some excitement in aluminium, due to January tightness, dealers said.
"Onc the (November) options were out of the way it (the copper market) just died on its feet. There was some covering after the options, but it was sat on above $1,970," one said.

Option declarations passed routinely in late morning, with most $2,000 calls declared, as well as a smattering of puts at this strike. But with the market still uncertain over inventory movements in the Far East, prices are expected to remain range-bound in the short-term, they said.
Last kerb business was at $1,971 a tonne, up $10 from Tuesday's kerb close.

The principal focus of attention in aluminium was on borrowing of the January date, which resulted in the overall cash/threes contango easing to $20/21 at one point from $26 on Tuesday. At the close it stood at $23.00/23.50.
Traders said there are heavy speculative shorts located in January, where metal is tightly held. Jan/one day traded at a premium of $6.
The influence on the forward market was modest, howver, with producer selling lurking overhead. Last business was at $1,434, up $2 from Tuesday.

The tin market briefly clocked up another 17-month low of $5,880 this morning, but subsequently staged a modest rally and regained $5,900. Technically, prices are oversold in the short-term, traders said.
However, with consumers still holding off, looking for an eventual dip to $5,800, there is little upside scope. Final business was at $5,925, up $20 from yesterday.

Nickel business mostly failed to excite, with the market well defended on dips towards $7,100. But with prices showing little inclination to move higher interest was generally restricted to little changed levels. Last trade was at $7,140, against Tuesday's close of $7,150.
Zinc continued to consolidate, with the momentum of last week having faltered, and unless there is a fresh influx of speculative buying the market may drift. Prices closed at an unchanged $1,062.50.
Lead's price movements were barely noticeable throughout a slow day, but there is an underlying upside bias to sentiment, due to the approach of winter. Final business was at $743, down $1.
Alloy was quiet, but the recent technical appreciation in prices was maintained with three months ending at $1,295/97, up from $1,280 yesterday.
